rapport_notes: Conversational but mechanical; no warmth, no personal connection established, mostly transactional delivery of pricing.
process_discipline_notes: No violations detected, but this is because critical steps were simply omitted entirely rather than duplicated.

evidence_quotes.agenda: Never asked. Rep launched directly into pricing explanation: 'Well, yeah, I do have the estimate here, I just wanna quickly, you know, go over how the pricing goes.'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: No concerns raised by customer to probe; rep asked no discovery questions about customer priorities, pain points, or move-specific concerns.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Not present. Rep gave estimates ($5,969 full service; $3,246 move-only) but never framed them as a window, never addressed what drives variance, never mentioned crew performance guarantees, prep tips, or locked-in rates.
evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Absent. Rep said 'I just wanna quickly...go over how the pricing goes' — no time-box, no framing of the exchange as 'a few questions in return for an accurate quote.'
evidence_quotes.close: Implicit end only. Customer said 'I will be giving you a call back when I get some more details then to lock in the date,' and rep replied 'Sounds good...I'll send you the email shortly.' No explicit rate-lock language; no direct ask ('would you like our help'); no confirmation of next steps beyond 'give us a call back.'

top_strength: Delivered clear, itemized pricing (hourly rates by day, packing material estimates, full-service vs. move-only comparison) and gave customer concrete numbers ($5,969 and $3,246) they requested, meeting the transactional expectation.
coaching_note: This call skipped all discovery entirely—no agenda question, no two-layer follow-up on customer priorities, no differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, communication)—and jumped straight to pricing delivery; build the trust and uncover needs before quoting, per the Call Map.
